sources.author: Harrison Chase
sources.headline: Co-founder & CEO @ LangChain
sources.post_summary: Discussed the rapid evolution of AI agents from simple chatbots to autonomous systems capable of multi-step reasoning and tool use. Highlighted how developer tooling around memory, planning, and execution loops is becoming critical infrastructure for production AI applications.

sources.author: Simon Willison
sources.headline: Independent AI researcher & creator of Datasette
sources.post_summary: Shared practical insights on building reliable AI automation pipelines, emphasizing the importance of observability and error handling in agentic workflows. Warned against overhyping current agent capabilities while acknowledging real productivity gains in developer tooling.

sources.author: Sarah Guo
sources.headline: Founder @ Conviction & AI investor
sources.post_summary: Analyzed the emerging AI infrastructure stack, comparing it to the early cloud computing era. Covered key investment themes around vector databases, model serving infrastructure, and evaluation frameworks needed to support production AI agents at scale.

sources.author: Andrej Karpathy
sources.headline: AI researcher & educator
sources.post_summary: Posted about the shift from monolithic models to composable AI systems where agents orchestrate multiple specialized tools. Discussed implications for developer experience and the need for better debugging and testing frameworks for agent-based applications.

sources.author: Elena Vasquez
sources.headline: Head of Revenue Operations at Attentive
sources.post_summary: Discussed how her team rebuilt their outbound motion by layering intent signals with automated sequences, cutting CAC by 23% while increasing reply rates. Emphasized the need for tight alignment between RevOps and GTM engineering to maintain data hygiene across tools.

sources.author: Marcus Chen
sources.headline: GTM Engineer at OpenAI
sources.post_summary: Shared a framework for building outbound automation systems that combine enrichment APIs, scoring models, and dynamic sequencing. Highlighted how his team reduced manual SDR work by 60% by engineering content triggers based on buyer signals.

sources.author: Priya Sharma
sources.headline: VP of Content Strategy at Notion
sources.post_summary: Explained how content strategy should be treated as a revenue channel, not just brand awareness. Detailed her approach to mapping content assets to specific stages of the buyer journey and measuring pipeline influence through attribution modeling.

sources.author: David Okonkwo
sources.headline: Director of Sales Operations at Ramp
sources.post_summary: Walked through how his team operationalized outbound at scale by building internal tooling that syncs CRM data with enrichment platforms and triggers personalized sequences. Stressed the importance of clean data flows between RevOps and marketing.

sources.author: Rachel Kim
sources.headline: Founder & CEO at Lavender
sources.post_summary: Shared lessons from building AI-powered outbound tools, focusing on how GTM teams can engineer better email deliverability and response rates through structured testing frameworks and real-time coaching embedded in workflows.

sources.author: Arpit Mohan
sources.headline: Founder & CEO at Attentive AI | Ex-Amazon
sources.post_summary: Shared his journey of building and shipping a new AI product feature in under 10 days as a solo founder. Highlighted the importance of rapid iteration, user feedback loops, and how he leveraged no-code tools to validate before full engineering effort.

sources.author: Danny Postma
sources.headline: Founder at Headlime & KeywordsReady | Indie Maker
sources.post_summary: Posted about pivoting from a failed SaaS idea to a new micro-SaaS built entirely solo. Detailed the tech stack, first 100 users acquired via Twitter/LinkedIn outreach, and revenue milestones reached within 6 weeks of launch.

sources.author: Vicente Herrera
sources.headline: Software Engineer | Building in Public | Ex-Google
sources.post_summary: Documented his transition from corporate engineering to full-time indie development. Shared weekly progress updates on his open-source dev tool, including GitHub metrics, user signups, and lessons from cold outreach to developers.

sources.author: Sara Mauskopf
sources.headline: Founder & CEO at Winnie | YC Alum
sources.post_summary: Wrote about the realities of solo-founder life while shipping a major product update. Covered tradeoffs between speed and polish, handling customer support alone, and how she maintains momentum without a full team.

sources.author: Alex West
sources.headline: Indie Developer & Creator | ex-Meta
sources.post_summary: Shared his experience leaving Meta to build a niche productivity app solo. Included transparent revenue numbers, tech choices (Next.js + Supabase), and how he used LinkedIn to find early beta users from his network.
